messages:
Jared: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands finance section, drop runway/procurement questions here and we'll reply.
Maya: TL;DR: cash runway ~18 months on base plan; downside scenarios and controls in the deck.
Priya: can you share the monthly burn split one-liner?
Maya: Monthly ~ $3.2M: payroll ~$1.4M, infra/GPU ~$1.25M, go-to-market ~$350k, other ~$200k (rounded).
Ravi: what's the new procurement approval matrix? last week a card charge slipped through.
Carlos: Updated matrix: P-cards allowed up to $1k per txn; manager approval for $1k-$5k; Director + Finance for $5k-$25k; >$25k requires Legal + CFO. Auto-hold for renewals > $15k.
Priya: any change to vendor auto-renew handling?
ProcurementBot: Auto-flagging enabled: renewals > $10k are flagged; renewals > $15k are put on temporary hold pending review. Owners notified via the portal.
Sofia: how about fast customer-impact buys? we've lost deals waiting for approvals.
FinanceOps: Expedited path: open procure ticket, mark "expedite_customer", include product owner + finance sponsor, and tag @Maya. Target triage within 24 hours for genuine customer-impact cases.
Maya: Also adding an "expedite approval pool": Finance will pre-approve up to $200k/month in aggregate for verified customer-impacting spend across teams. Teams must register spend in the ticket.
Ravi: are we changing delegated manager budgets to avoid blocking SRE/infra work?
Carlos: Managers retain small delegated budgets: $1k for tooling; Directors can approve $1k-$5k with Finance CC'd. For infra-critical items we recommend the expedite flow.
Priya: any plans to buy GPUs (capex) vs cloud?
Maya: We're running TCOs for two pilot racks to support steady Dedicated capacity. Any single capex > $200k requires ROI analysis + board notification.
Jared: Important: no compensation changes today. Our aim is surgical operating controls, not across-the-board cuts.
Sofia: who owns exceptions if a vendor invoice arrives and it's >$25k but contract signed earlier?
ProcurementBot: Owner of the contract must open an emergency review ticket, attach the signed contract, and tag @Carlos + @Maya. Finance will clear or place a one-time approval hold within 48 hours.
Ravi: SLA expectations? last quarter some PO approvals took 3 weeks.
FinanceOps: New SLA targets: <$1k: same business day; $1k-$5k: 2 business days; $5k-$25k: 5 business days; >$25k: 10 business days. Use "expedite_customer" for faster handling.
Priya: will teams need to reforecast?
Maya: Yes 3 All teams: submit Q2 reforecast by EOD next Friday. Use the updated finance template in Confluence (#finance-docs).
Carlos: We'll also publish a short procurement playbook with examples (PO vs p-card vs contract) and a recommended approvals checklist.
Sofia: any changes to capitalized purchases policy?
Maya: Capitalization unchanged, but capex proposals need an upfront TCO and expected utilization. Capex > $200k triggers board notice.
Jared: External comms? customers asking about stability.
Maya: No external comms planned 1 internal only. If anything materially changes we'll coordinate a customer message via Sales.
Ravi: who to reach for 1:1 finance questions?
Maya: Office hours Wed 10-11am and Fri 3-4pm PT, and Slack #finance-ops for async. For urgent approvals use the procurement ticket flow.
Priya: thanks everyone 44d closing the thread.
Carlos: Docs + approval matrix will be posted to #finance-docs and Confluence. Reach out for walk-throughs.
